scenes.title: Value at Risk (VaR) vs. Expected Shortfall (ES / CVaR)

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare VaR Threshold: measures the point loss cutoff but ignores the magnitude of catastrophic losses beyond the cutoff, vulnerable to rogue trader exploitation ([fact-01], [fact-10]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Expected Shortfall: averages all losses exceeding VaR, satisfying subadditivity and directly measuring tail severity ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Equal-Weighting Flaw: standard historical simulation treats past volatile periods identically to calm periods ([fact-09]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Volatility Scaling Formula: r_t* = r_t * (sigma_current / sigma_t) scaling past returns to match current market volatility environments ([fact-09]).

summarySteps: 1. Value at Risk (VaR) ([fact-01]): The dollar loss amount V not exceeded with confidence X over N days.
2. Subadditivity Failure ([fact-02]): VaR fails the subadditivity axiom, meaning combined portfolio VaR can exceed the sum of individual VaRs.
3. Expected Shortfall (ES) ([fact-03]): Coherent risk measure quantifying expected loss conditional on exceeding VaR.
4. FRTB Regulatory Shift ([fact-04]): Basel Committee replaced 10-day 99% VaR with 10-day 97.5% Expected Shortfall to capture tail risk.
5. Historical Simulation ([fact-05]): Subjects current portfolio to actual percentage price changes observed over past M trading days.
6. Table 20.1 Calculation ([fact-07]): Average of the 5 worst scenario losses yields an Expected Shortfall of $282,204.
7. Hull-White Volatility Updating ([fact-09]): Scaled historical returns r_t* = r_t * (sigma_current / sigma_t) capture current elevated volatility.
8. Basel Backtesting ([fact-11]): Validates 99% 1-day VaR models over 250 trading days using Green, Yellow, and Red Traffic Light zones.
bottomTakeaway: While Value at Risk provides a baseline percentile loss, Expected Shortfall offers a coherent measure of tail risk that underpins modern FRTB capital frameworks and historical simulation risk management ([fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05]).
